result_text:
Tickets now carry an optional support agent, and every ticket list and lookup you named returns it. The ticket test classes pass (29 tests, `BUILD SUCCESS`).

What changed:

- **`schema.sql`**: `support_ticket` has a new nullable `agent VARCHAR(100)` column.
- **`model/SupportTicket.java`**: new last record component `agent` (null when unassigned). I kept the old 9-argument constructor so existing callers, tests included, still compile.
- **`DataStore.java`**: `createSupportTicket` writes the agent. The 9 ticket queries you listed (lookup by number, customer, priority, region, sales rep, customer-with-order, old high-priority by region, open on date, product) select `agent` and map it into the record.
- **`service/SupportTicketService.java`**: `create` has an overload taking an agent (blank becomes null). The existing 6-argument `create` delegates with no agent. `changeStatus` copies the agent into the returned ticket. The status update SQL doesn't touch the column, so the agent survives in the database too.

Decisions to check:
- The agent is a plain name string on the ticket, not a separate support-agent table, since the task didn't mention one.
- The new parameter is the last one on `create`, and the field is called `agent`.
- Existing tests only exercise the old signatures, so no test asserts an agent value. I didn't add one to keep the change small; say if you want a round-trip test for "Sam" and the unassigned case.

Nothing is committed.
